rows.claim: Admin::EmbeddingController#update discards the request payload entirely and re-renders the current state, making PUT /admin/customize/embedding a persistence no-op that returns success. The admin-embedding controller's saveChanges action is wired to this endpoint, so any future settings UI or API client that PUTs embedding attributes receives a 200 while nothing is saved — an inert endpoint that should either accept attributes or not be routed.

The `_hydrateEmbedded` regex broadened from `/(.+)\_id$/` to `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`, so every existing payload key matching `*_ids` — which previously passed through untouched as a raw id array on the record — is now intercepted, hydrated via `_lookupSubType`, moved to the pluralized key, and the raw `*_ids` key is deleted. Any existing client code reading `record.get('some_ids')` on a serialized payload silently gets hydrated model objects (or an empty array) instead of ids after this change; the change was introduced for the embedding feature's `embeddable_host_ids` but rewrites hydration behavior for the entire store, a coupling the PR title does not surface.

The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout/AbortSignal, making it a timeout-less outbound call on the token-refresh path which executes inside user-facing booking and calendar operations. The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is issued with no timeout or AbortSignal, yet it sits inline on the request path of every calendar and video operation once the feature is enabled. A hung or slow parent endpoint (mid-deploy restart, network partition) stalls each affected booking/calendar request for up to undici's default multi-minute header/body timeouts instead of failing fast, and concurrent requests pile up against the parent, degrading every booking that touches a synced app.

The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT on the token-refresh request path has no timeout, no response.ok/status check, and no payload-size bound. If the sync endpoint hangs, every booking involving a shared credential stalls indefinitely (all callers await this promise with no AbortController); if it returns a non-JSON error page, downstream parsers throw an unrelated 500, masking the real failure.

The findFirst-then-create sequence is a check-then-insert race with no UNIQUE(userId, appId) constraint backing it (the in-code claim that upsert is impossible is exactly the missing unique key), and the (userId, appId) slot also has a second writer in the local OAuth callback. Two concurrent webhook deliveries (e.g., a reconnect racing an in-flight sync) both miss the findFirst and create duplicate Credential rows for the same user and app, and the findFirst can also overwrite the key of a locally-installed credential; consumers binding to a stale duplicate use dead tokens.

The findFirst-then-create sequence runs without a transaction and Credential has no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent syncs both take the create path, and the unordered findFirst thereafter updates a nondeterministic row. Overlapping initial syncs create duplicate credentials for the same user and app, and later syncs update only one of them, leaving a stale credential that booking flows can still select - producing intermittent 401s that survive every re-sync.

The function unconditionally replaces a missing refresh_token with the placeholder string "refresh_token" before the parsed result is persisted to prisma.credential by callers. The Google refresh path persists the entire zod safeParse wrapper — `{success, data}` — as `credential.key`, because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the raw safeParse result while the code it replaces stored the flat output of `googleCredentialSchema.parse()`. The Google token refresh persists the zod safeParse wrapper as the credential key: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full SafeParseReturnType ({success, data}) but `data: { key }` stores that wrapper object instead of `key.data`. The stored credential becomes {success:true,data:{...}}, so on the next load googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) throws (access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date are now nested under .data) and every Google Calendar operation for that user fails; the refresh itself reports success, so credentials are silently corrupted for all deployments (no env flags required) within ~1 hour of deploy and require manual DB surgery or user re-auth.

The hand-rolled Salesforce token refresh is not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely, unlike every other integration in this diff. With the feature off, every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation now performs an eager token-endpoint round-trip plus a credential-table write on the path jsforce previously refreshed lazily (extra remote call + DB write on every availability/booking operation); with the feature on, Salesforce never consults CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, so it is the one OAuth app the sync feature silently does not cover.

Google's refresh now persists parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, ...) instead of schema.parse(googleCredentials) on the pre-existing credential object, so under credential-sharing mode the loose minimum schema replaces the strict googleCredentialSchema validation of the entire stored key. The handler runs appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) with no try/catch and never checks req.method, so input errors throw instead of returning the 4xx the surrounding code deliberately uses for every other input problem. The handler runs appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and then JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...)) with no try/catch, so a malformed body or a payload encrypted with a mismatched key throws out of the handler. The parent application receives a raw 500 (Next's unhandled route error) instead of the 4xx JSON every sibling branch of this endpoint returns, so it cannot distinguish a bad payload from a broken Cal.com deployment — retries loop on the 500 and integration debugging has no message to work with.

The handler runs appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) with no HTTP method guard and no error handling, and the later JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is equally unprotected. The handler trusts the parent's raw numeric userId to identify the local user (the schema comment says 'UserId of the cal.com user') with no cross-instance identity mapping or verification such as an email check. Unless the child instance's user id space is kept identical to cal.com's, the webhook delivers one cal.com user's OAuth credentials to the local user holding the same numeric id — a different person — who then books meetings through another user's calendar; any user created or deleted on either side diverges the id spaces and nothing in the design detects it.

The handler validates the body with throwing `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (not safeParse) and no try/catch, so any malformed body — or any GET, whose body is undefined — throws ZodError out of the handler. Malformed webhook deliveries get an unhandled 500 instead of the 4xx this handler's own contract uses for client errors (403/404 JSON), and senders that retry 5xx will retry the poison payload indefinitely.

The sync branch returns the raw fetch Response object without calling .json(), while several wired adapters expect library-shaped return values (google-auth-library's res, axios's AxiosResponse, hubspot's parsed HubspotToken). The sync branch returns the raw fetch Response while all seven call sites were written against the provider-specific shapes the default branch returns (gaxios res.data for Google, a HubspotToken object for HubSpot, an axios response with .data for Zoho CRM/Bigin, provider-envelope JSON for the Lark/Zoom/MS handlers). The sync branch returns the raw `fetch` Response whose body is whatever the credential-sync endpoint produces (documented as 'only the access token and expiry date'), but every call site (Lark, Zoom, Webex, Office365, Zoho) immediately consumes the response with provider-specific parsing/handleErrors helpers, and the Google call site reads `res?.data` off the Response object. /embed/best accepts anonymous GETs and unconditionally enqueues RetrieveTopic, with throttling keyed only per embed_url (the redis key retrieved:<url>), not per client or IP. An attacker iterates embed_url=http://host/<random-path> — each unique path passes the embeddable_host check and defeats the per-URL 60-second throttle — to enqueue unbounded jobs that each create a junk topic under embed_by_username with skip_validations, flooding the sidekiq queue and the site's topic lists with scraped garbage from a plain curl loop.

add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1 backfills every existing post with the value 1, but Post.cook_methods = Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) assigns sequential values starting at 0, so the default 1 maps to :raw_html instead of :regular. Every pre-existing post is reclassified as raw_html and every newly created regular post inherits the same column default (PostCreator only assigns cook_method when the option is passed, so all normal posts get the default), so Post#cook returns raw markdown site-wide: any edit or recook persists uncooked markdown into the cooked column and the rendering pipeline (markdown, emoji, oneboxes) silently disappears for all content.

add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1 sets every existing post to cook_method=1, which per Post.cook_methods Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) is :raw_html. After this migration runs, every pre-existing post in the database is silently reclassified as raw HTML: Post#cook (app/models/post.rb:131-134) returns raw uncooked text for cook_method == :raw_html, so all historical markdown posts render their raw markdown source to users. The default should be 0 (:regular); the migration backfills the entire table with the wrong value and there is no correcting backfill step.

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls String#scrub, which does not exist on the Ruby this app runs (the Gemfile states the project targets 1.9; String#scrub shipped in Ruby 2.1), so poll_feed raises NoMethodError on every execution. With feed_polling_enabled, the hourly job crashes before importing anything, so feed-based embedding never imports a single item. Additionally the loop has no per-item rescue, so even on a Ruby with scrub, one item with nil content (plain RSS 2.0 description-only feeds) or nil title aborts all remaining items for that run, every run.

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element (nil), and `sidekiq_options retry: false` ensures the run is not retried. Any feed containing a single summary-only or content-less item (common for Atom feeds with only <summary>) makes every hourly poll die at that item, so all articles after it are never imported and the feature fails silently with no retry and no error surfaced to the operator.

cook returns raw unfiltered for cook_method raw_html, and the RSS path (Jobs::PollFeed → TopicEmbed.import) never passes content through readability's tag whitelist — that whitelist exists only in import_remote — so third-party feed HTML is stored as cooked with zero sanitization. A malicious or MITM-compromised feed (open() happily fetches plain http) stores <script>/<iframe>/onerror payloads that render verbatim via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb and in normal Discourse topic views — stored XSS executing on the Discourse origin and every embedding page with viewers' sessions; spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb even asserts cooked == raw, codifying the unsanitized behavior as accepted without any security sign-off.

cook_method == raw_html returns the post raw, bypassing the entire sanitize/render pipeline, and TopicEmbed.import sets this for all externally-fetched RSS/article content, which is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in embed views. Any attacker-controlled markup in the polled feed or in a page fetched by TopicRetriever (script tags, event handlers, javascript: hrefs) is stored and rendered unsanitized on /embed/best — a persistent XSS executing in the embeddable_host origin, the origin that third-party sites iframe by design. skip_validations: true on both create and revise removes the last guard.

create_table :topic_embeds, force: true bakes a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS into the migration, so once the table holds production data any re-run silently destroys the embed_url-to-topic mapping. After this ships, a re-run triggered by a schema_migrations/restore mismatch drops every topic_embeds row; TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed then returns nil for known URLs, so the next retrieve/poll re-imports each article and creates a duplicate topic while the original topic and its replies remain on the forum, doubling content until the mapping is manually rebuilt.

Both external fetches (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` here and `open(url).read` in TopicEmbed.import_remote) use open-uri with no open/read timeout. A stalled or slow-loris feed/article server hangs the sidekiq thread indefinitely (open-uri has no default open timeout); with retry: false the hourly poll slot is consumed by the hung thread and repeated hangs exhaust the sidekiq worker pool, stalling unrelated background jobs on the instance.

create_table :topic_embeds, force: true on a table with null: false topic_id/post_id columns drops any pre-existing topic_embeds table on re-run. If this migration is ever re-run (db:migrate:redo, or a partially-migrated environment where the table already exists with imported topic/post associations), all topic_embed rows are silently dropped, orphaning every imported topic from its source URL so feed polling re-imports duplicates and embed lookups 404.

Jobs::PollFeed passes each RSS item's body straight into TopicEmbed.import after only CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) — no filtering, with the entity-decode re-arming escaped payloads — where it is stored as raw HTML. Anyone who can influence a single feed item — a compromised or aggregating third-party feed source, or an attacker-modified setting value — gets markup stored and rendered unsanitized in every viewer's session in the forum, including admins, on an hourly schedule.

`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` executes the entire feed poll synchronously inside the retrieve_topic sidekiq job, but PollFeed's execute guard re-checks `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` — already true — and `poll_feed` then does a blocking `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` network fetch plus a PostCreator DB write per item, all inside a job whose sole purpose is to fetch one URL. Each first-time embed request triggers a full-feed import inside the retrieve_topic worker; a large feed makes the worker block for minutes and hammers the third-party feed server on every new embedded URL, and if the feed fetch raises (e.g. timeout) the RetrieveTopic job fails with retry instead of falling through to fetch_http.

Both success-path specs verify only mock invocations - 'TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})' returns nil and 'retriever.expects(:retrieve)' - and run without render_views, so the rendered output of embed/best (the posts loop, the empty-posts start_discussion branch in app/views/embed/best.html.erb, and app/views/embed/loading.html.erb's reload path) is asserted by nothing in the diff (checked spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the only spec touching the endpoint). A feed_polling_url of `|<command>` (config-backed sink; treat the settings store as attacker-influenceable input) executes arbitrary commands on the app server during the hourly poll — remote code execution, not merely SSRF.

The user-selector offers existing members for selection, so an admin re-adding one triggers the failure; combined with the client's missing rejection handler the 500 is swallowed and the Add button appears to do nothing.

The update context retains only the automatic-group case and deletes the old "is able to update group members" spec, so the non-automatic mainline of the new update action (renaming via params[:name], alias_level, and visible persistence — the path every admin Save click exercises) has no assertion anywhere in the diff. A regression in admin group rename/settings persistence (for example the group.name assignment or the visible == "true" coercion) ships with a green suite, because the single remaining update spec only asserts the automatic-group branch.

This diff deletes the 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' and 'succeeds silently when removing non-members' tests, but the replacement add_members/remove_member actions retain the silent-skip behavior with no replacement assertion anywhere in the rewritten spec (the only test file changed for this controller). add_members still skips unknown usernames without error (and now also silently skips whitespace-padded entries because usernames.split(',') is never stripped) and remove_member no-ops on a non-member user_id; nothing pins that contract, so a future change to 422 on unknown users — or a bug that silently drops real members — ships undetected.

This diff deletes the PATCH-era tests that explicitly covered silent edge behavior ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users', 'succeeds silently when removing non-members') but the replacement endpoints retain both behaviors untested: add_members skips nonexistent usernames via `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` (groups_controller.rb add_members) and remove_member's `group.users.delete(user_id)` silently no-ops for a non-member id. An admin who typos a username in the new Add-members input gets a 200 success response and the client reloads a member list that never grew — with no test in the diff asserting that silent-skip is intentional, a future refactor that makes a missing user raise (or partially apply) would pass CI while changing real admin-facing behavior.

This group-memberships PR also restyles the badges admin form: the label/input-width rules were deleted from section.details .form-horizontal and re-added only under a new ".groups, .badges" scope, which is work not traceable to the stated intent. Any admin page that relied on the deleted section.details .form-horizontal rules without a .groups or .badges ancestor class (the badges details form, if its markup lacks a .badges wrapper) silently loses its 350px input widths and bold labels, and badges styling now changes in lockstep with unrelated group styling.

Three new tests hard-code id 1 / group_id: 1 (the .update test anchored here, plus the 'cannot add members' and 'cannot remove members' examples) and depend on seeded automatic groups instead of fabricating one the way the sibling .destroy test does with Fabricate(:group, automatic: true). The 422 assertions verify test-database seed state as much as controller behavior: if automatic groups are not created before these examples run, or their ids shift, Group.find(1) raises RecordNotFound or a non-automatic group 1 fails the assertions with diagnostics unrelated to the code under test.

totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing a phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and showingLast on that page. An admin paging a 100-member group with limit 50 sees "1/3"; clicking next lands on an empty third page where next is still not disabled, and the previous "showingLast" guard never fires on the real last page when offset math drifts.

With create and update no longer assigning group.usernames, the Group model's usernames= full-list membership sync keeps no caller on the HTTP surface, leaving two parallel membership mechanisms — the dead model-level sync and the new add_members/remove_member endpoints. The usernames accessor and its sync callback become dead machinery the next contributor must discover is unused before changing membership semantics, and it silently rots instead of being deleted.

`{{#unless automatic}}` in the group-member item view template resolves `automatic` against the item view's context — the member (a Discourse.User), which has no `automatic` property — instead of the group the surrounding group.hbs template binds. The remove control renders on every member row of automatic groups (admins, moderators, trust_level_*), where the server forbids removal — clicking it shows a bootbox confirm and then always fails with an error response, presenting an action the system cannot perform.

add_members calls group.add(user) for every CSV username with no check that the user is already a member, and the client never clears the add-members input after a successful add (the author's own TODO), so re-submitting an existing member inserts a second group_users join row. An admin who clicks the Add button again (the stale username is still in the input) or who types the name of someone already in the group creates a duplicate membership: the user appears twice in the member list, user_count is inflated (group.users.count counts join rows), and cleanup requires manual DB deletion; there is no unique index on group_users to raise an error.

add_members calls group.add(user) for every supplied username with no check that the user is already a member, and the admin UI's addMembers action deliberately leaves the usernames input populated after a successful add (the in-code TODO), so clicking Add twice re-submits the same usernames. Re-adding an existing member inserts a second group_users row (member listed twice, user_count inflated) or raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique for a 500, and the admin receives no feedback in either case; no spec in the diff covers duplicate adds.

add_members resolves each username via `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` and silently skips non-matching names, then returns success_json regardless of how many adds actually happened. An admin who submits 'bob,alice' where alice is a typo or a renamed account gets a success response and a reloaded list showing only bob — the partial failure is indistinguishable from success, with no error, count, or per-name feedback.

add_members calls `group.add(user)` with no existing-membership check before pushing into the users association. Re-adding a user who is already a member — the natural case, since addMembers never clears the input and has no in-flight guard against double-clicks — raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique from the join-table insert and returns a 500, with usernames earlier in the comma list already inserted, leaving partially-applied membership and no indication to the admin.

add_members calls params.require(:usernames).split(",") without type coercion, so a request whose usernames parameter is a JSON array raises NoMethodError (undefined method `split' for Array) and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx. API clients sending usernames as an array — the shape the old PATCH changes:{add:[...]} endpoint accepted — get an unhandled 500 from this admin endpoint rather than a validation error.

add_members calls usernames.split(",") on params.require(:usernames) without any type check, so a request carrying usernames as an array (JSON body {"usernames":["a","b"]} or form field usernames[]=a) raises NoMethodError (undefined method 'split' for Array) and returns a 500. Any consumer of this .json admin API endpoint that naturally passes the usernames as an array gets a 500 Internal Server Error instead of a 2xx/4xx; the admin UI (comma-joined string) never triggers it, so the defect stays hidden until an API client appears.

addMembers has the same defect: the .then calls self.findMembers() without returning it, detaching the reload's failure from the promise chain. After a successful add, a failed refresh leaves the newly added member invisible in the list with no error, so the admin cannot tell whether the add took effect.

add_members reads `params.require(:group_id)`, but the route added for it (config/routes.rb:49-50, a bare `put 'members'` inside the admin `resources :groups` block) is a member route that supplies the group key as `params[:id]`, so every real request raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns 400. Every 'add members' click in the admin UI sends PUT /admin/groups/:id/members.json and receives a 400; no member is ever added through the shipped UI, the rejected promise has no handler anywhere on the path (model addMembers, controller action), so the admin gets zero feedback and the feature is dead on arrival — the controller specs pass only because `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: ...` bypasses routing entirely.

add_members silently skips every username that does not resolve to a user (User.find_by_username returns nil) and then renders success_json, reporting success for the dropped work. An admin who submits a misspelled username — or a pasted list like 'bob, alice' where the space after the comma breaks find_by_username — receives a 200 and a reloaded member list without the member: no error, no log, no indication which name failed, so the add appears accepted and simply does nothing.

addMembers silently succeeds when some or all submitted usernames do not match any user, returning success_json with nothing added and no indication of which names were skipped. An admin typos 'johm' instead of 'john', gets a green success response, the member list reloads unchanged, and the admin has no way to know the add failed — membership drifts silently.

add_members splits the usernames string and issues one User.find_by_username query per username inside the loop (N+1), with no batched WHERE username IN (...) lookup. Adding a large batch of members issues N sequential user lookups plus N group.add association writes instead of a batched load and one save; on an admin action over a big paste this scales linearly per-user at DB roundtrip cost.

Admin::GroupsController#remove_member looks up the group with `Group.find(params[:id].to_i)` — the line carried over unchanged from the old `destroy` action — but the new member route `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` inside `resources :groups` binds the group id as `params[:group_id]`, and both the client (`Discourse.Group#removeMember` requesting `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`) and the diff's own specs supply `group_id`, never `id`. In every real request `params[:id]` is nil, so `Group.find(0)` raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound and the endpoint returns 404 — the admin UI's remove-member button never removes anyone — and both new specs (`xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: group.id, ...` expecting success, and `group_id: 1` expecting 422) fail against this code.

After removeMember on the last member of a page, findMembers clamps offset against the stale user_count (set from the previous fetch), fetches a page past the new end, and the stale offset is then persisted, leaving the UI stuck on an empty page. Removing the final member of the last page shows an empty member list with pagination controls reading a bogus currentPage/totalPages; the admin must click previous to recover, and the meta.total/user_count the next() clamp relies on was stale at request time.

addMembers ships with an in-code TODO ("should clear the input") acknowledging the user-selector is never cleared after a successful add. After adding a batch the stale usernames stay in the input, so the admin must manually clear them before the next batch and a second click of Add re-sends the same names; the field itself never confirms the add happened.

After removeMember, findMembers clamps the offset against the still-stale client-side `user_count` (it is only updated from the response's meta), so the request goes out with an offset equal to the old count and the server echoes it back in `meta.offset`, leaving the UI on an empty page beyond the new last page. An admin on the last page who removes the final visible member (e.g. 51 members, offset 50, remove the last one) sees an empty list with a pager reading past the real page count; recovery requires manually clicking previous.

create() no longer accepts or sends usernames, so the long-standing ability to add initial members at group-creation time is silently removed from the admin flow. Previously an admin could create a group and seed its membership in one step (createWithUsernames); now they must create the group, wait for it to persist, then add members separately — a user-facing workflow regression introduced by iteration without explicit acceptance of the capability removal.

findMembers attaches no rejection handler to the Discourse.ajax promise, and both callers (routes' setupController and the pager actions) invoke it fire-and-forget without returning/propagating it, so any server failure is swallowed. When /groups/:name/members.json returns an error, the user sees an empty member list (or the previous page's stale list after next/previous) with no error message; the rejected promise is unhandled and the failure is invisible.

findMembers builds the request URL from the live `name` property, which is two-way bound to the editable name text-field on the admin group form, so paginating or adding members after editing the name (before saving) queries a group name that does not exist. An admin who types a new name and then clicks next/previous or Add triggers GET /groups/<edited-name>/members.json, which 404s; the member list silently fails to refresh, so addMembers appears to do nothing even though the PUT succeeded.

findMembers clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, offset), which permits offset == user_count — a page past the last member — instead of capping at user_count - limit. Removing the last member while the final page holds exactly one member (e.g. a 51-member group on page 2) reloads with offset still at 50 against a new total of 50, leaving the admin staring at an empty '2/2' member list until they manually click 'previous'.

findMembers clamps the request offset against the pre-fetch user_count and then writes the server-echoed meta.offset back into the model, so an offset that was valid before a removal is preserved on a page that no longer exists. With 51 members (limit 50), removing the single member shown on page 2 reloads at offset 50 against the now-50-member group, stranding the admin on an empty "2/2" page even though 50 members remain, recoverable only by clicking previous.

findMembers returns undefined (bare 'return ;') when the group name is empty, and the request itself is fired before result.meta is validated — the caller awaiting it (previously the route's afterModel) now receives undefined instead of a promise. Any caller that chains on findMembers() for an unnamed group gets undefined and crashes with a TypeError on .then; on the meta path, if the response lacks meta (server error shape change), result.meta.total throws inside the then handler, surfacing as an unhandled rejection rather than a user-visible error.

members passes params[:offset].to_i and (params[:limit] || 50).to_i straight into .offset()/.limit() with no validation, so negative values reach SQL as OFFSET -1 / LIMIT -1. GET /groups/{name}/members.json?offset=-1 makes PostgreSQL raise its 'must not be negative' error as ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and the request returns a raw 500 instead of a 4xx for the malformed parameter.

members passes params[:offset].to_i straight into the SQL offset without clamping, so a negative offset (e.g. offset=-1) generates invalid SQL and a 500 on the public /groups/:name/members endpoint. Any client (including anonymous ones, subject to visibility) sending a negative offset triggers an ActiveRecord/Postgres error instead of a 4xx, producing error noise and a 500 response.

next commits group.set("offset", offset) before the findMembers() request resolves — and previous does the same at line 46 — with no rollback and no rejection handler, so a failed request leaves the committed offset in place. When the members request fails after clicking next, currentPage (derived from the pre-committed offset) shows page 2 while the member list still renders page 1's data, and no error is surfaced anywhere — the page indicator and the list content disagree with no way to tell the request failed.

addMembers ships with the acknowledged 'TODO: should clear the input' — the user-selector retains the just-added usernames after the Add action succeeds. The next Add click re-submits the previous usernames along with any new ones (e.g. 'alice,bob' when only bob was intended), so every subsequent add carries stale members whose re-addition is either a silent no-op or a server error depending on Group#add's dedup behavior.

next/previous commit group.set("offset", offset) before findMembers() resolves, with no rollback on failure and no in-flight guard, so pagination bookkeeping is updated for requests that may fail or complete out of order. A failed page fetch leaves the page label advanced while the list still shows the previous page, and the next click silently skips a page; two rapid clicks issue overlapping requests whose out-of-order responses overwrite the newer page with older members because setProperties runs whenever a response lands.

offset = params[:offset].to_i (and likewise limit) is passed straight into ActiveRecord's offset/limit without clamping, so a negative value such as ?offset=-1 produces 'OFFSET -1' SQL that PostgreSQL rejects with an error, returning a 500. Any client — including anonymous visitors, since this is a public endpoint — can force a 500 on a group members page with one malformed query parameter; previously the offset param was only honored for automatic groups and ignored for manual ones.

offset = params[:offset].to_i is passed to .offset() with no lower clamp, so a client-supplied negative offset reaches PostgreSQL as OFFSET -n. GET /groups/<name>/members.json?offset=-1 raises 'OFFSET must not be negative' (ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid) and returns an HTML 500 on this public endpoint instead of a 4xx; the Ember client clamps its own offset, but any API consumer sending a negative value gets a 500.

Pagination math is off by one: totalPages = Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 yields 3 pages for 100 users at limit 50, and next() clamps offset to Math.min(offset+limit, user_count) (e.g. 101 for user_count=101), which requests a page with zero members. For any group whose member count is an exact multiple of the limit, showingLast never becomes true and the admin can page into an empty last page; for non-multiples, the clamp lands past the last page start so the final page renders an empty member list while displaying currentPage/totalPages as valid.

removeMember and addMembers attach only a .then handler with no .catch, and the reload inside .then (self.findMembers()) is not returned, so every failure in the mutation chain — the DELETE/PUT itself or the follow-up reload — is an unhandled rejection. An admin who clicks the remove (×) icon or Add and the request fails (422 for automatic groups via API race, 404, 500) sees the bootbox confirm succeed and then nothing happens: no error message, member list unchanged, failure completely invisible; the controller's addMembers/removeMember actions (admin-group.js.es6 lines 51-65) also discard the returned promise, so even a caller-level catch would not help.

removeMember and addMembers attach only a .then that reloads the member list, with no .catch; a 422 (e.g. can_not_modify_automatic) or network failure leaves the UI showing the pre-operation member list with no feedback. An admin clicks remove/add on a group whose mutation is rejected; bootbox confirm closed, no error rendered, list unchanged — the user-facing operation fails invisibly.

removeMember and addMembers call self.findMembers() inside .then without returning it, so a failure of the member-list reload is an unhandled promise rejection that leaves the previously rendered member list in place with no error surfaced. After a successful add/remove, if the follow-up findMembers request fails (network drop, 500), the admin still sees the pre-operation member list — e.g. a removed member still appears after a confirmed removal — with no error dialog; the rejection also propagates as an unhandled promise rejection.

removeMember and addMembers have no rejection handling anywhere in the chain — the model methods attach no .catch, the inner self.findMembers() reload is neither returned nor caught, and the controller actions discard the returned promises — so a failed membership mutation is invisible. When the PUT/DELETE to /admin/groups/<id>/members.json fails (500, dropped connection), the admin who clicked Add or the remove × sees nothing: no error, no state change, no pending indicator; and even after a successful mutation a failed reload leaves the stale member list with no signal, so the admin cannot tell whether the membership changed.

removeMember and addMembers invoke `self.findMembers()` inside their `.then` without returning it and with no rejection handler, while the controller actions (admin-group.js.es6:56, 64) drop the returned promises entirely. The outer promise resolves success before the member list reload even starts, and when any link in the chain fails (a 4xx on add/remove, an expired session, a failed reload) the rejection is swallowed with no handler anywhere — the admin receives zero feedback and the member list silently shows stale state.

remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) followed by group.save, but the diff removes the patch-based incremental delete path (update_patch) that the old specs verified ('can make incremental deletes', 'succeeds silently when removing non-members') without any replacement coverage for non-existent user_ids. The new DELETE endpoint has no spec for removing a user who is not a member (or a non-existent user_id), so a regression in GroupUser join-row deletion would ship unnoticed; group.save on an association mutation is also a no-op placeholder that hides whether deletion actually failed.

remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) then group.save and returns success_json even when the user was never a member, and group.save is a no-op on an unchanged record so validation cannot report the miss. A request with a stale or wrong user_id gets a 200 success while no membership was removed; the admin UI (which reloads the list and trusts the response) treats the no-op as a confirmed removal, hiding the real state from the operator.

remove_member reads `params.require(:group_id)` while its route (config/routes.rb:49, bare `delete 'members'` inside the admin `resources :groups` block) supplies the group key as `params[:id]`, so every real removal request raises ActionController::ParameterMissing and returns 400. The admin confirms the bootbox dialog, the DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json returns 400, the member is never removed, and the unhandled rejection means nothing is shown — the remove link appears to do nothing for every non-automatic group, undetectable by the controller specs which pass `group_id:` directly.

removeMember reloads the list via findMembers without adjusting offset, and findMembers clamps offset against the stale pre-fetch user_count (line 23), so removing the last member of the last page reloads to an empty page. With 51 members (limit 50) the admin on page 2 removes the single listed member; the reload requests offset 50 against the new total of 50, gets zero members back, and the admin is stranded on an empty '2/2' page until clicking previous.

removeMember reloads via self.findMembers() with the offset unchanged, so when a removal empties the current page the server returns an empty list for a now-past-the-end offset and nothing adjusts the page back. With 51 members, page 2 shows one member; removing that member leaves the admin staring at an empty '2/2' page that looks like the member list was wiped until they click previous.

remove_member replaces the model's removal path (the deleted update_patch used group.remove(user)) with group.users.delete(user_id), which deletes the group_users join rows via a callback-free delete on the has_many :through association, so any bookkeeping the model performs on membership removal (user_count maintenance, GroupUser destroy callbacks) never runs. After every member removal the group's persisted user_count stays inflated (and destroy-callback cleanup is skipped), so the public groups list and the admin pagination show too many members and phantom pages until the count is recomputed; the removal spec only asserts group.users.count == 0 so it cannot catch this.

remove_member silently no-ops (and returns success) when user_id is not a member of the group, and group.save on an untouched record can never fail so the 422 branch is dead. A stale UI or double-invocation sends a user_id that was already removed; the endpoint returns success, the client reloads and shows the member still present or the removal 'succeed' with nothing done — no error distinguishes a real removal from a no-op.

removeMember's success callback reloads via findMembers(), which clamps offset against the stale pre-removal user_count and then adopts the server-echoed offset, so nothing pulls the pager back when the member count shrinks across a page boundary. With 101 members and the admin on page 3, removing that page's single member reloads offset=100 against the 100 remaining members and renders an empty member list labeled '3/3' — the admin must notice and click previous before any member is visible.

Same regression as the admin route: setupController calls model.findMembers() without returning or catching the promise, replacing afterModel's awaited version. On the public group members page, a failed members request leaves the table permanently empty with no error shown to the user, and the rejection propagates as an unhandled promise rejection instead of the route error handling the afterModel version exercised.

setupController fires model.findMembers() without returning the promise or attaching any rejection handler, so a failed fetch leaves the public group members page silently empty. A user viewing /g/<name>/members when the members request fails (403 after the group was made invisible, 500, network drop) gets an empty member table with no error; the removed afterModel propagated the rejection and aborted the transition, so the failure was visible before this diff.

The '.add_members cannot add members to automatic groups' test hardcodes group_id: 1 without creating any group, relying on the assumption that group id 1 is automatic. If the test database's group with id 1 is not automatic (e.g. after fixture/seed changes or when another spec deletes/recreates groups), the request succeeds with 200 and the assertion response.status.should == 422 fails — or worse, passes vacuously through a different error path. The same applies to the remove_member automatic test at lines 126-129, which additionally issues a PUT (xhr :put, :remove_member) even though the route/action semantics are DELETE, so the test no longer matches the HTTP verb the client and router actually use.

addMembers and removeMember chain only .then() with no rejection handler, so a 422 from can_not_modify_automatic (or any validation failure on group.save) leaves the UI in its prior state with no client-side indication of failure. Admins clicking 'Add' or the remove 'x' on a group the server refuses get a silent no-op (beyond whatever global ajax error flash Discourse shows); combined with the always-rendered remove control on automatic groups, this produces clicks that appear to do nothing.

add_members silently skips any username that does not match a user and still renders success_json, so a partially-applied batch is indistinguishable from a successful one. An admin who submits 'alice,bob' with a typo sees the member list reload without bob and no error anywhere; the only documentation of this behavior was the 'succeeds silently' tests this diff deletes.

The '.remove_member cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec issues xhr :put against a route defined only as delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", so the request cannot reach the action. The spec raises an ActionView::MissingExactRoute/ActionController::RoutingError (or hits an unintended route) and fails, meaning the automatic-group guard for removal is not actually tested by this suite.

The '.remove_member' happy-path test issues xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route is delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", so the PUT is routed to add_members with usernames nil and params.require(:usernames) raises before remove_member ever runs. The test fails (ActionController::ParameterMissing / 400 response instead of success), and if it were passing it would be passing for the wrong action — the actual remove_member happy path is never exercised.

The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test issues xhr :put against an endpoint whose only route is delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'. The PUT does not match any route, so the request raises an ActionController::RoutingError before reaching the controller; the test never exercises remove_member's automatic-group guard (response is a routing failure, not the asserted 422), so the guard on the delete path is unverified.

The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test issues xhr :put to remove_member, but the only route wired to remove_member is DELETE 'members' (routes.rb), so the PUT matches add_members instead. The PUT request routes to Admin::GroupsController#add_members, where params.require(:usernames) raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, returning a 500 — the spec's expectation of 422 fails, so the shipped test suite is red and the automatic-group guard for remove_member is never actually exercised.

The addMembers action fires this.get("model").addMembers(...) without returning or catching the promise, and never clears the usernames input (the in-code TODO), so a failed PUT is swallowed and the stale names remain in the field. An admin clicks Add, the request fails (network error/500), nothing is added and no error is shown; the input still holds the old names so the next click silently re-submits the same list, compounding the invisible failure.

The addMembers action neither returns the model.addMembers promise nor has any in-flight guard or input clearing, so concurrent invocations interleave and the committed input state desyncs from the server. Double-clicking the Add button issues overlapping PUT requests; and because the username input is never cleared after a successful add (the TODO), the same usernames remain in the selector and are re-submitted on the next click, while the controller gives the caller no promise to observe success/failure — a failed add leaves the input populated as if it had been consumed.

The `automatic` guard in group_member.hbs resolves against the member item context (a Discourse.User), not the group, and User has no `automatic` property. The remove ('x') link renders on every member row even when viewing an automatic group; clicking it issues DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members which the server rejects with 422, so the admin gets an unexplained error on a control that should never have been shown.

The automatic-group protection test for remove_member issues xhr :put but the route is registered as DELETE, so the request does not match the route under test. The spec never exercises the can_not_modify_automatic guard for remove_member; it passes/fails on routing behavior, leaving the 422 path for member removal untested.

The create action changed its accepted envelope from nested params[:group][:name]/[:usernames]/[:visible] to flat params[:name]/[:visible], silently discarding the usernames field. Existing API consumers posting group[name]=x&group[usernames]=a,b get a 200 with a created group that has none of the requested members — the old create seeded membership atomically with creation and this behavior is gone with no error or version bump, so callers believe members were added.

add_members silently skips any username that does not match an existing user (User.find_by_username returns nil and the iteration continues), then reports success_json. An admin who typos one of several usernames gets a success response and a reloaded list missing that user with no error, so the failed add is invisible unless they recount the roster; the old PATCH path had the same flaw but this diff enshrines it in the new dedicated endpoint.

The GET /admin/groups/users endpoint is deleted from the admin namespace with no replacement registered in this diff, breaking any existing client or integration still calling it. Out-of-tree consumers (API scripts, plugins) that listed admin group users via GET /admin/groups/users now get a 404 with no deprecation path.

The GET /admin/groups/users route is deleted and the PATCH-style incremental membership update (update_patch with changes[:add]/[:delete]) is removed in the same diff, breaking the previously supported admin group API surface without deprecation. Out-of-tree consumers (scripts, API integrations, plugins) using GET /admin/groups/users or PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes silently get 404s/routing failures after upgrade — an objective change (redesign of membership API) with no migration path or acceptance call-out.

The item view template tests {{#unless automatic}}, but the view is rendered with the member (Discourse.User) as its context via itemView="group-member" in group.hbs, so `automatic` resolves against the User object (which has no such property) and is always falsy — the remove link renders for members of automatic groups. On automatic groups (admins, etc.) every member row shows the 'x' remove control; an admin who clicks it gets a bootbox confirm, a DELETE that the server rejects with 422 can_not_modify_automatic, and no visible feedback that nothing happened.

the members endpoint applies no upper bound to the client-supplied limit param (limit = params[:limit].to_i with no max), so a request with limit=1000000 loads and serializes the entire member table. Any visitor who can see the group can request an arbitrarily large limit, forcing a full-table query and an unbounded serialized JSON payload on the request path — memory/latency exhaustion with no cap.

The members endpoint passes params[:offset].to_i straight into the SQL offset clause without clamping, so offset=-1 produces a negative OFFSET that PostgreSQL rejects. A request to /groups/:name/members.json?offset=-1 raises ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid and returns a 500 instead of a 4xx, breaking any caller that paginates backwards past zero.
